answer: Every agent must lock a bond inside an on-chain vault before its attestation is counted, and the required bond scales with how many identities already share its operator footprint. A sybil swarm therefore pays a rising price per key, while a single honest node pays only the base rate. Bonds of keys later proven linked are slashed to the commons, so faking ten identities costs more than running one real agent. Reputation, like a comet, is only visible when it drags real mass through the tundra of sunk cost; names are cheap, collateral is not.
